chapters.n: John, an eyewitness Apostle, opens like his Gospel: he writes about Jesus, the Word of life who existed from the beginning. He stresses that the Apostles heard, saw, and even touched Him—Jesus was truly flesh.

f.g: Christ, the living message of God.

chapters.n: In a side note, John explains that eternal life—Christ Himself, who was with the Father—became visible, and the Apostles testify of Him.

f.g: Made visible, revealed.

chapters.n: John shares his witness so readers can join the Apostles in fellowship—a fellowship that is really with the Father and the Son.

f.g: Greek koinōnia — sharing, partnership, communion.

chapters.n: He writes so that their joy—and his—may be complete.
The core message: God is light, with no darkness at all. Light stands for truth, goodness, and holiness.
If we claim closeness to God while living in sin, we are lying and not living by the truth.
But if we live in God’s light, we have true fellowship with each other, and Jesus’s blood keeps cleansing us from every sin.

f.w: blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us

chapters.n: Claiming we have no sin is self-deception. Honesty about our weaknesses is where repentance begins.
A promise to treasure: if we confess our sins, God is faithful and fair to forgive us and wash away all wrongdoing.
Denying that we have ever sinned effectively calls God a liar, since His word says all need a Savior.
Tenderly calling them “little children,” the aged John writes to help them avoid sin. But if anyone sins, Jesus Christ the Righteous pleads our case before the Father.

f.g: Greek paraklētos — one called alongside to help, like a defense attorney.

chapters.n: Jesus is the atoning sacrifice for our sins—and not only ours, but the whole world’s.

f.g: An offering that removes sin and restores a right relationship with God.

chapters.n: How can we know we truly know God? By keeping His commandments.
Anyone who says “I know Him” but ignores His commandments is a liar.
In those who obey His word, God’s love reaches its full purpose. That’s how we know we are united with Him.

f.g: Brought to completion.

chapters.n: Whoever claims to abide in Christ should live as He lived.
This commandment isn’t new; it’s the old one they heard from the start—the command to love.
Yet it is also new, because in Christ it is fully lived, and His light is now pushing away the darkness.
Anyone who claims to be in the light but hates a fellow believer is still in darkness.
Whoever loves others stays in the light and has nothing in him to make himself or others stumble.

f.g: Something that trips a person up.

chapters.n: Hatred blinds. Someone who hates walks around in the dark without knowing where he is going.
John writes to all believers, his “little children,” because their sins are forgiven through Christ’s name.
In a poetic pattern, John addresses believers at different stages: mature “fathers” who know the eternal Christ, “young men” who have overcome the evil one, and children who know the Father.

f.g: Satan.

chapters.n: He repeats and expands his words: the fathers know the eternal One; the young men are strong because God’s word lives in them, and they have defeated the evil one.

f.w: word of God abideth in you

chapters.n: Don’t love the world’s system and its values. Love for the world crowds out love for the Father.
John names three worldly pulls: bodily cravings, greed for what we see, and arrogant pride in possessions or status. None of them come from the Father.

f.g: Boastful pride in one’s possessions or position.

chapters.n: The world and its cravings are fading away, but whoever does God’s will lives forever.
It is the last hour. They had heard that antichrist would come, and already many antichrists—people opposing Christ—have appeared.

f.g: One who opposes or replaces Christ.

chapters.n: These opponents had left the Church. Their leaving showed they had never truly belonged.

f.g: Likely early teachers who denied Jesus truly came in the flesh.

chapters.n: Faithful believers have been anointed by the Holy One—a reference to the Holy Ghost—and so they can know the truth.

f.g: Anointing—here the gift of the Holy Ghost.

chapters.n: John writes not because they don’t know the truth, but because they do, and they know no lie comes from truth.
The real liar is the one who denies Jesus is the Christ. Denying the Son is denying the Father too.

f.w: denieth that Jesus is the Christ

chapters.n: No one who denies the Son has the Father; whoever acknowledges the Son has the Father as well. The brackets mark words the KJV translators added in italics.
Hold on to the gospel you heard from the start. If it stays in you, you will remain in the Son and the Father.
And Christ’s promise to us is eternal life.
John writes this to warn them about those trying to lead them astray.

f.g: Mislead, lead astray.

chapters.n: The Holy Spirit they received stays with them and teaches them truth. That doesn’t mean teachers are useless, but that the Spirit confirms what is true.

f.w: ye need not that any man teach you
f.g: Not rejecting teachers, but trusting the Spirit over false teachers.

chapters.n: Remain in Christ, so that when He appears we can stand confident rather than ashamed at His coming.

f.g: Boldness, freedom of speech.

chapters.n: Since Christ is righteous, everyone who does what is right shows that he has been born of God.
Look at the amazing love the Father has given us: we are called children of God! The world doesn’t recognize us because it didn’t recognize Him.

f.g: What astonishing, foreign-to-this-world kind of love.

chapters.n: We are God’s children now, and what we will become hasn’t been fully shown. But when Christ appears we will be like Him, because we will see Him as He is.
Everyone with this hope makes himself pure, just as Christ is pure.
Sin is breaking God’s law—choosing lawlessness over His will.

f.g: Greek anomia — lawlessness.

chapters.n: Christ came to take away our sins, and in Him there is no sin.
Whoever remains in Christ does not keep on sinning; one who persists in sin has not really known Him. The JST renders this as not ‘continuing’ in sin.

f.g: Greek present tense: does not keep on sinning as a lifestyle.

chapters.n: Don’t be fooled: doing what is right is what makes a person righteous, as Christ is righteous.
The person who lives in sin belongs to the devil, who has sinned from the start. The Son of God came to destroy the devil’s works.

f.w: destroy the works of the devil

chapters.n: Those born of God don’t continue in sin, because God’s life is planted in them. The JST reads that the Spirit of God remains in him and he cannot continue in sin.

f.g: God’s life-giving nature or Spirit planted within.

chapters.n: Here is how you can tell God’s children from the devil’s: anyone who doesn’t do right or doesn’t love others is not from God.
From the very beginning the message has been: love one another.
Don’t be like Cain, who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother. He did it because his own deeds were evil and Abel’s were good.
So don’t be surprised if the world hates you.
Our love for fellow believers is evidence that we have passed from spiritual death into life. Without love, we remain in death.
Anyone who hates his brother is a murderer at heart, and no murderer has eternal life living in him.
We understand love by this: Christ gave His life for us. So we should be willing to give our lives for others.

f.w: laid down his life for us

chapters.n: If someone has plenty and sees a brother in need but closes his heart, how can God’s love be in him?

f.g: In ancient thought the inner organs were the seat of feelings—our ‘heart.’

chapters.n: Let’s not love only with words or talk, but with real actions and sincerity.
Loving through actions assures us that we belong to the truth, and it calms our hearts before God.

f.g: Reassure, persuade our hearts.

chapters.n: Even when our own heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart and knows everything—including our sincere desires.

f.w: God is greater than our heart

chapters.n: And when our heart doesn’t condemn us, we can approach God with confidence.
We receive what we ask from Him because we keep His commandments and do what pleases Him.
His commandment is twofold: believe in the name of His Son Jesus Christ, and love one another.

f.w: believe on the name of his Son

chapters.n: Those who keep His commandments live in Him and He in them. The Spirit He has given us is how we know He is with us.

f.w: by the Spirit which he hath given us

chapters.n: Don’t trust every spiritual claim. Test whether a message really comes from God, because many false prophets are out in the world.

f.g: Test them, as metal is tested.

chapters.n: Here is one test: any spirit that acknowledges Jesus Christ came in a real human body is from God. Some false teachers claimed Jesus only seemed to have a body.

f.g: Against early teachers (often called Docetists) who denied Jesus had a real physical body.

chapters.n: Any spirit that denies this is not from God—it is the spirit of antichrist, which they were warned about and which is already at work.
You belong to God and have overcome these false teachers, because the One in you is greater than the one in the world.

f.w: greater is he that is in you

chapters.n: False teachers belong to the world, speak its language, and so the world listens to them.
We Apostles are from God; those who know God listen to us. This is how we can tell the Spirit of truth from the spirit of error.
Dear friends, let’s love one another, because love comes from God. Everyone who truly loves is born of God and knows Him.
Anyone who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, because God is love—love is His very nature.
God showed His love by sending His Only Begotten Son into the world so we could live through Him.
Real love isn’t that we loved God first, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.

f.g: The sacrifice that removes sin and reconciles us to God.

chapters.n: If God loved us that much, we should love one another.

f.w: we ought also to love one another

chapters.n: No one has seen God at any time, but when we love one another, God lives in us. The JST adds “except them who believe,” leaving room for prophets who have seen God.

f.w: No man hath seen God at any time

chapters.n: We know we live in Him and He in us because He has given us His Spirit.
The Apostles have seen and testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Savior of the world.
Whoever openly confesses that Jesus is the Son of God has God living in him, and he lives in God.
We have come to know and trust God’s love for us. God is love; whoever lives in love lives in God, and God in him.
Love made complete in us gives us confidence on judgment day, because in this world we are becoming like Christ.

f.w: boldness in the day of judgment

chapters.n: There is no fear in love; perfect love drives fear out. Fear is tied to punishment, so anyone still afraid has not yet fully grown in love.

f.g: Punishment, or the dread of it.

chapters.n: We love because He loved us first. Our love is always a response to God’s.
If someone says “I love God” but hates his brother, he’s lying. If you can’t love a person you can see, how can you love God, whom you can’t see?
His command is clear: whoever loves God must love his brother too.
Everyone who believes Jesus is the Christ is born of God. And if you love the Father, you will love His children too.
We know we truly love God’s children when we love God and keep His commandments.
Loving God means keeping His commandments—and His commandments aren’t a crushing burden.

f.g: Heavy, burdensome.

chapters.n: Everyone born of God overcomes the world, and our faith is the victory that does it.
Who can overcome the world? Only the one who believes Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus came “by water and blood”—likely His baptism and His death. Against teachers who said the divine Christ left before the cross, John insists He came through both. The Spirit confirms this truth.

This verse names the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost as heavenly witnesses who are one. Many scholars note it is missing from the earliest Greek manuscripts; Latter-day Saints understand the Godhead as one in purpose.

f.g: Latter-day Saints read this as unity of purpose among three distinct beings.

chapters.n: On earth, three witnesses agree: the Spirit, the water, and the blood. Under the law of Moses, truth was established by two or three witnesses.
We accept human testimony; God’s testimony about His Son is far greater.
Whoever believes in the Son has that testimony inside himself. Refusing to believe God’s witness of His Son is calling God a liar.
God’s testimony is this: He has given us eternal life, and this life is in His Son.
Whoever has the Son has life; whoever doesn’t have the Son doesn’t have life. It is that simple.
John states his purpose: he writes so believers can know they have eternal life and keep believing in Christ’s name.
We can be confident that if we ask anything that matches God’s will, He hears us.
And if we know He hears us, we know we have what we asked—in His way and timing.

f.g: Requests.

chapters.n: Pray for a believer who sins in a way not leading to death, and God will give him life. There is a sin leading to death, and John doesn’t ask for prayers for it—probably deliberate, total rejection of Christ.
All wrongdoing is sin, but not every sin leads to spiritual death. Repentance remains open.
Those born of God don’t keep living in sin; the Son of God protects them, and the evil one cannot get hold of them.

f.g: Many manuscripts read ‘keeps him,’ meaning Christ protects the believer.
Cannot seize or harm him.

chapters.n: We know we belong to God, while the whole world lies under the power of the evil one.

f.g: Lies in the power of the evil one.

chapters.n: The Son of God has come and given us understanding so we can know the true God. We are in Him through Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life.
John’s closing words: little children, keep away from idols—anything that takes God’s place in your heart.
